answer:
Promptfoo has no dedicated "one provider at a time" setting. Instead, you limit overall concurrency to 1, which runs every provider's test cases sequentially.

**Command line:**

```bash
promptfoo eval --max-concurrency 1
```

or the short form:

```bash
promptfoo eval -j 1
```

**In your config file** (e.g. `promptfooconfig.yaml`):

```yaml
evaluateOptions:
  maxConcurrency: 1
```

The CLI flag should override the config value. I'm fairly confident of these option names, but I'm not certain of the exact spelling in every version, so check `promptfoo eval --help` if the flag isn't recognized.

If you need providers to run in a strict sequence and not just one request at a time, the concurrency limit is the closest built-in option I know of. I don't know of a way to make Promptfoo finish all cases for one provider before starting the next.
